title: A paged sequence
description:
Use `yield return` to read data a page at a time and a disposable timer to measure it.

```
page 1: 1 2 3 4
page 2: 5 6 7 8
page 3: 9 10
loaded 3 pages lazily
took 0 ms
```
hints: Fill a `List<T>`; when it reaches `size`, `yield return list.ToArray();` and clear it. After the loop, yield what is left (lesson 4.05).
`Timed` starts a `System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch` in its constructor and prints `ElapsedMilliseconds` in `Dispose` (lesson 4.04).
requirements: `IEnumerable<int> FetchAll(int total, int pageSize)` yields items one by one, and loads (prints) a new page only when it is needed.
`IEnumerable<T[]> Pages<T>(IEnumerable<T> items, int size)` groups any sequence into arrays (without LINQ's `Chunk`).
`class Timed : IDisposable` prints the time when disposed; use it with `using`.
stretch: Show that `FetchAll(1000, 10).Take(15)` loads only two pages.
